q: प्रसिद्ध 'महान स्नानागार' और काँस्य निर्मित 'नर्तकी की मूर्ति' किस सिंधु घाटी स्थल से उत्खनित हुई थी?
e:
Both the Great Bath (made waterproof with bitumen/gypsum) and the lost-wax bronze 'Dancing Girl' were discovered at Mohenjo-daro (Larkana, Sindh, excavated by R. D. Banerji in 1922) (मोहनजोदड़ो से महान स्नानागार व नर्तकी की काँस्य मूर्ति मिली)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. 'Mohenjo-daro' literally means 'Mound of the Dead' (मृतकों का टीला) in Sindhi.
2. Harappa yielded the famous 'Granary' (6+6 rows), Cemetery H, and R-37 burials.
3. Surkotada (Gujarat) yielded the only widely cited Harappan remains of horse bones.
qe: The iconic 'Great Bath' (महान स्नानागार) and the bronze figurine of the 'Dancing Girl' were excavated from which Indus Valley site?

q: राजस्थान के किस हड़प्पा स्थल से विश्व के प्राचीनतम जुते हुए खेत (दोहरी फसल प्रणाली के हल रेखाओं सहित) और अग्निवेदिकाओं के साक्ष्य मिले हैं?
e:
Kalibangan (Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan, Ghaggar river, excavated by B. B. Lal and B. K. Thapar) revealed ploughed fields, fire altars, and mud-brick houses (कालीबंगा से जुते हुए खेत व अग्निवेदिकाएँ मिलीं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. 'Kalibangan' literally means 'Black Bangles'.
2. Banawali (Haryana, excavated by R. S. Bisht) yielded a terracotta replica of a plough (मिट्टी का हल).
3. Lothal and Kalibangan both showed evidence of fire altars.
qe: Which Harappan site in Rajasthan yielded the world's earliest known ploughed agricultural field (with double-crop furrow pattern) and fire altars?

q: उत्तर प्रदेश (प्रतापगढ़ जिला) के किस पुरातात्विक स्थल से दमदमा और महदहा के साथ मध्यपाषाणकालीन मानव कंकालों, अस्थि आभूषणों और चूल्हों के साक्ष्य प्राप्त हुए हैं?
e:
Sarai Nahar Rai, Mahadaha, and Damdama in Pratapgarh district (UP) are landmark Mesolithic sites of the Ganga Plains showing early burials and bone tools (सराय नाहर राय, महदहा और दमदमा उत्तर प्रदेश के प्रमुख मध्यपाषाण स्थल हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Bagor (Rajasthan) and Adamgarh (MP) provide the earliest Mesolithic evidence of domestication of animals (~5000 BCE).
2. Atranjikhera (Etah, UP) is famous for early Iron Age / Painted Grey Ware (PGW) remains.
3. Chopani Mando (Prayagraj, UP) yielded some of the earliest hand-made pottery in the world.
qe: Which archaeological site in Uttar Pradesh (Pratapgarh district) has yielded Mesolithic evidence of human skeletons, bone ornaments, and hearths, alongside Damdama and Mahadaha?

q: सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता में मानक घनाकार चर्ट बाट (weights) निचले मानों में किस प्रमुख गणितीय अनुपात प्रणाली का अनुसरण करते थे?
e:
Lower denominations of Harappan weights were binary (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64), while higher denominations followed the decimal system with multiples of 16 (हड़प्पा बाट द्विआधारी प्रणाली 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 के गुणजों में थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Harappan urban planning used a strict gridiron street layout with baked bricks in the standardized ratio 4 : 2 : 1 (length : breadth : thickness).
2. Mesopotamian cuneiform records refer to the Indus Valley region as 'Meluhha' (मेलुहा).
3. Dilmun (Bahrain) and Magan (Oman) served as intermediate maritime trade hubs between Meluhha and Mesopotamia.
qe: In the Indus Valley Civilization, the standard cubical chert weights followed which predominant mathematical ratio system in lower denominations?

q: गुजरात का कौन-सा हड़प्पा स्थल सामान्य दो भागों के बजाय अनूठे रूप से तीन किलेबंद भागों (दुर्ग, मध्य नगर और निचला नगर) में विभाजित था?
e:
Dholavira (Kutch, Gujarat, excavated by R. S. Bisht) had a three-tier town plan, monumental stone reservoirs, and a 10-sign Harappan signboard inscription (धोलावीरा तीन भागों में विभाजित एकमात्र हड़प्पा नगर था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Dholavira was inscribed as India's 40th UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2021.
2. Rangpur (Gujarat) yielded rice husk evidence from the Late Harappan phase.
3. Harappan civilization's mature urban phase spanned roughly 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE.
qe: Which Harappan site in Gujarat is uniquely divided into THREE fortified parts (Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town) instead of the usual two?

q: चारों वेदों में सबसे प्राचीन वेद कौन-सा है, जिसमें 10 मण्डलों में संगठित 1,028 सूक्त हैं?
e:
Rigveda (~1500–1000 BCE) is the oldest Vedic text, recited by the 'Hotri' priest (ऋग्वेद सबसे प्राचीन वेद है, जिसमें 10 मण्डल व 1,028 सूक्त हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Priests of the four Vedas: Rigveda — Hotri; Samaveda — Udgatri (music/chants); Yajurveda — Adhvaryu (rituals/sacrifices); Atharvaveda — Brahma (charms, medicine).
2. 'Sabha' (council of elders) and 'Samiti' (general assembly) were called the 'two daughters of Prajapati' in the Atharvaveda.
3. Rigvedic economy was primarily pastoral; cow ('Aghanya' — not to be killed) was the chief measure of wealth.
qe: Which of the four Vedas is the oldest and consists of 1,028 hymns (Suktas) organized into 10 Mandalas?

q:
सूची-I (ऋग्वैदिक नदी नाम) को सूची-II (आधुनिक नाम) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. वितस्ता
2. अस्किनी
3. परुष्णी
4. विपाशा
सूची-II:
(a) ब्यास
(b) रावी
(c) चिनाब
(d) झेलम
e:
Vitasta = Jhelum, Askini = Chenab, Parushni = Ravi, Vipasha = Beas (and Shutudri = Sutlej, Sadanira = Gandak, Kubha = Kabul) (1-d, 2-c, 3-b, 4-a)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Saraswati ('Naditama' — best of rivers) was the most sacred river of the Rigveda, while Sindhu (Indus) was mentioned most frequently.
2. Ganga is mentioned only once and Yamuna thrice in the Rigveda.
3. The Battle of Hydaspes (326 BCE, Alexander vs Porus) was fought on the banks of the Vitasta (Jhelum).
qe:
Match List-I (Rigvedic River Name) with List-II (Modern Name) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Vitasta
2. Askini
3. Parushni
4. Vipasha
List-II:
(a) Beas
(b) Ravi
(c) Chenab
(d) Jhelum

q: बौद्ध धर्म में 'त्रिरत्न' (Three Jewels) क्या हैं?
o: Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct
e:
In Buddhism, Triratna consists of Buddha, Dhamma (teachings), and Sangha (monastic order); in Jainism, Triratna consists of Samyak Darshana (Right Faith), Samyak Jnana (Right Knowledge), and Samyak Charitra (Right Conduct) (बौद्ध धर्म के त्रिरत्न बुद्ध, धम्म और संघ हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Four major events of Buddha's life: Birth (Lumbini — Lotus/Bull), Renunciation (Mahabhinishkramana — Horse), Enlightenment (Bodh Gaya — Bodhi Tree), First Sermon (Sarnath — Wheel), Mahaparinirvana (Kushinagar — Stupa).
2. The Eightfold Path (Ashtangika Marga) forms the Fourth Noble Truth (path to end suffering).
3. Buddha's teachings were delivered primarily in Pali (Magadhi Prakrit) so common people could understand them.
qe: In Buddhism, what are the 'Three Jewels' (Triratna / त्रिरत्न)?
oe: Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct

q: मगध के हर्यक वंश का वह शासक कौन था जिसने गंगा और सोन नदियों के संगम पर पाटलिपुत्र (कुसुमपुर) नगर की स्थापना की?
e:
Udayin (son of Ajatashatru) founded Pataliputra and made it the capital of Magadha (उदायिन ने पाटलिपुत्र की स्थापना कर उसे राजधानी बनाया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Bimbisara (founder of Haryanka dynasty, capital Rajagriha) sent his royal physician Jivaka to treat King Pradyota of Avanti.
2. Ajatashatru ('Kunika') used two innovative war weapons—Rathamusala and Mahashilakantaka—against the Lichchhavis of Vaishali.
3. Mahapadma Nanda ('Ekarat', 'Sarvakshatrantaka') founded the Nanda dynasty; Dhana Nanda was overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya.
qe: Who was the ruler of the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha who founded the city of Pataliputra (Kusumapura) at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers?

q: मगध में 12 वर्षीय अकाल के बाद जैन धर्म किन दो आचार्यों के नेतृत्व में मुख्य रूप से दिगम्बर और श्वेताम्बर सम्प्रदायों में विभाजित हुआ?
e:
Bhadrabahu led followers south to Shravanabelagola (Karnataka, accompanied by Chandragupta Maurya) forming the Digambara tradition, while Sthulabhadra stayed in Magadha leading the Shvetambara tradition (भद्रबाहु दिगम्बर व स्थूलभद्र श्वेताम्बर परंपरा के प्रमुख थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Chandragupta Maurya performed 'Sallekhana' (ritual fasting unto death) at Shravanabelagola.
2. The 57-feet monolithic statue of Gomateshwara (Bahubali) at Shravanabelagola was commissioned by Ganga minister Chamundaraya (~981 CE).
3. Jain canonical texts (Agamas) were composed mainly in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.
qe: The Jain sect split into Digambara (sky-clad) and Shvetambara (white-clad) primarily under the leadership of which two monks following a 12-year famine in Magadha?

q: सेल्यूकस निकेटर का कौन-सा यूनानी राजदूत पाटलिपुत्र में चन्द्रगुप्त मौर्य के दरबार में रहा और जिसने 'इंडिका' की रचना की?
e:
Megasthenes served as Seleucus Nicator's ambassador to Chandragupta Maurya (~302–298 BCE) and wrote 'Indica', describing Mauryan society as divided into 7 classes (मेगस्थनीज ने 'इंडिका' लिखी)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Deimachus (ambassador of Antiochus I) visited Bindusara's court; Dionysius (from Ptolemy II of Egypt) visited Bindusara/Ashoka.
2. Bindusara was called 'Amitrochates' (Amitraghata — Slayer of Foes) by Greek writers and patronized the Ajivika sect (founded by Makkhali Gosala).
3. Pliny wrote 'Naturalis Historia' lamenting the drain of Roman gold to India for luxury spices and textiles.
qe: Which Greek historian and ambassador of Seleucus Nicator lived at the court of Chandragupta Maurya in Pataliputra and authored 'Indica'?

q: प्रसिद्ध 'साँची स्तूप' (मध्य प्रदेश) का मूल निर्माण सम्राट अशोक ने ईंटों से कराया था, जिसे बाद में किस राजवंश के काल में पत्थर से विस्तारित किया गया?
e:
During the Shunga period (2nd century BCE), Sanchi Stupa was encased in stone and expanded to double its original size, and its four intricately carved gateways (Toranas) were added under the Satavahanas (शुंग काल में साँची स्तूप का पाषाण विस्तार हुआ)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Ashoka's Dhamma Mahamattas (appointed in his 14th regnal year, Major Rock Edict V) propagated moral welfare across the empire.
2. The Rummindei Pillar Inscription (Lumbini, Nepal) records Ashoka's pilgrimage to Buddha's birthplace and reduction of land revenue (Bhaga) from 1/6th to 1/8th.
3. Barabar Caves (Bihar) were donated by Ashoka to the Ajivika ascetics.
qe: The famous 'Sanchi Stupa' (Madhya Pradesh, UNESCO World Heritage Site) was originally commissioned in brick by Emperor Ashoka and later enlarged in stone during which dynasty?

q: किस सातवाहन शासक को उसकी माता गौतमी बलश्री द्वारा उत्कीर्ण नासिक प्रशस्ति में 'एकब्राह्मण' और 'शक-यवन-पह्लव निसूदन' कहा गया है?
e:
Gautamiputra Satakarni (c. 106–130 CE), the greatest Satavahana ruler, defeated Shaka king Nahapana and restored Satavahana glory (गौतमीपुत्र शातकर्णी को नासिक प्रशस्ति में एकब्राह्मण कहा गया है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Satavahanas were the earliest rulers in India to make tax-free land grants (Brahmadeya) to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks, and issued mainly lead (सीसा) and potin coins.
2. Satavahana king Hala authored the famous Prakrit poetry anthology 'Gatha Saptashati'.
3. Satavahanas followed matronymic naming (using mother's name as prefix) while maintaining patrilineal succession.
qe: Which Satavahana ruler is celebrated in the Nasik Prashasti (composed by his mother Gautami Balashri) as 'Ekabrahmana' and 'Destroyer of the Shakas, Yavanas, and Pahlavas'?

q: चीन, मध्य एशिया और रोमन साम्राज्य को जोड़ने वाले 'रेशम मार्ग' (Silk Route) के भारतीय खंड पर किस राजवंश का प्रमुख नियंत्रण था?
e:
The Kushanas (especially Kanishka, capitals Purushapura/Peshawar and Mathura) controlled key branches of the Silk Route, bringing immense trade prosperity and gold bullion into India (कुषाणों ने रेशम मार्ग पर नियंत्रण रखा)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Kujula Kadphises founded the Kushana dynasty in India; Vima Kadphises was the first Kushana ruler to issue gold coins (depicting Lord Shiva & Nandi).
2. The 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea' (anonymous 1st-century Greek sailor's guide) details thriving Indo-Roman maritime trade via Barygaza (Bharuch), Muziris (Kerala), and Arikamedu (Puducherry).
3. Sangam literature (Tamil, 3 Sangams at Madurai under Pandyas) comprises works like Tolkappiyam, Silappadikaram (Ilango Adigal), and Manimekalai (Sattanar).
qe: The 'Silk Route' trade connecting China, Central Asia, and the Roman Empire was prominently controlled in North India by which dynasty?

q: राजा एंटियाल्किडास के किस इंडो-ग्रीक राजदूत ने लगभग 113 ई.पू. में बेसनगर (विदिशा, म.प्र.) में प्रसिद्ध 'गरुड़ स्तंभ' स्थापित किया और स्वयं को 'भागवत' घोषित किया?
e:
Heliodorus erected the Besnagar Garuda Pillar at the court of Shunga king Bhagabhadra—the earliest archaeological monument testifying to Bhagavatism (Vaishnavism) in India (हेलियोडोरस ने विदिशा में गरुड़ स्तंभ स्थापित कराया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Indo-Greeks were the FIRST rulers in India to issue portrait coins with kings' names and gold coins (die-struck).
2. King Kharavela of Kalinga (Chedi dynasty) is known from the Hathigumpha Inscription at Udayagiri (Odisha).
3. Ashvaghosha wrote 'Buddhacharita' (biography of Buddha in Sanskrit), 'Saundarananda', and 'Sariputraprakarana'.
qe: Which Indo-Greek ambassador of King Antialcidas erected the famous 'Garuda Pillar' (Heliodorus Pillar) at Besnagar (Vidisha, MP) around 113 BCE, declaring himself a 'Bhagavata' (devotee of Vasudeva)?

q: गुजरात और मालवा के पश्चिमी शक क्षत्रपों को पराजित करने के बाद किस गुप्त सम्राट ने प्रसिद्ध 'विक्रमादित्य' की उपाधि धारण की?
e:
Chandragupta II (375–415 CE, also called 'Shakari' — destroyer of Shakas) defeated Shaka ruler Rudrasimha III, issued silver coins, and presided over the Navaratnas at Ujjain (चन्द्रगुप्त द्वितीय ने विक्रमादित्य की उपाधि धारण की)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Sri Gupta founded the Gupta lineage; Chandragupta I (319–320 CE) started the Gupta Era and assumed 'Maharajadhiraja'.
2. The Iron Pillar of Mehrauli (Delhi), famous for its rust-resistant metallurgy, belongs to Chandragupta II's era.
3. The Gupta Age is termed the 'Classical Age' / 'Golden Age' of ancient Indian art, science, and Sanskrit literature.
qe: Which Gupta emperor adopted the celebrated title 'Vikramaditya' after defeating the Western Shaka Kshatrapas of Gujarat and Malwa?

q: गुप्तकालीन प्रसिद्ध नाटककार कौन थे जिन्होंने 'मुद्राराक्षस' (चाणक्य और चन्द्रगुप्त मौर्य की राजनीतिक कथा) और 'देवीचन्द्रगुप्तम्' की रचना की?
e:
Vishakhadatta authored both 'Mudrarakshasa' (unique Sanskrit play without a female lead) and 'Devichandraguptam' (describing how Chandragupta II rescued Dhruvadevi from Shaka humiliation) (विशाखदत्त ने मुद्राराक्षस व देवीचन्द्रगुप्तम् लिखा)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Amarasimha (one of the Navaratnas) compiled the famous Sanskrit lexicon 'Amarakosha'.
2. Vishnu Sharma authored the 'Panchatantra' fables during the Gupta era.
3. Sushruta and Vagbhata ('Ashtanga Hridaya') contributed profoundly to Indian medicine.
qe: Who was the famous Gupta-era playwright who authored 'Mudrarakshasa' (a political thriller about Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya) and 'Devichandraguptam'?

q: किस गुप्त सम्राट ने मध्य एशियाई हूणों के भयंकर आक्रमणों को सफलतापूर्वक विफल किया, जिसका उल्लेख जूनागढ़ और भीतरी स्तंभ अभिलेखों में मिलता है?
e:
Skandagupta (455–467 CE) decisively repulsed the Huna onslaught and repaired the Sudarshana Lake embankment (through governor Parnadatta and his son Chakrapalita) (स्कन्दगुप्त ने हूणों को पराजित किया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Later Huna chiefs Toramana and his son Mihirakula ravaged North India in the 6th century until defeated by Yashodharman of Malwa and Narasimhagupta Baladitya.
2. In Gupta taxation, 'Vishti' referred to forced labour (बेगार).
3. Tamralipti (Bengal) on the east coast and Bhrigukachchha (Bharuch) on the west coast were premier Gupta maritime ports.
qe: Which Gupta emperor successfully repelled the fierce Central Asian Huna invasions (led by Toramana/Hephthalites), as celebrated in the Junagadh and Bhitari inscriptions?

q: हर्षवर्धन के शासनकाल (606–647 ई.) में कन्नौज (643 ई.) में आयोजित प्रसिद्ध बौद्ध धर्मसभा, जिसकी अध्यक्षता ह्वेनसांग ने की, मुख्यतः किसके सम्मान हेतु थी?
e:
Harsha convened the grand Kannauj Assembly (643 CE) to honour Xuanzang and showcase the supremacy of Mahayana Buddhism, followed by the 6th quinquennial charity festival (Mahamoksha Parishad) at Prayaga (कन्नौज सभा महायान बौद्ध धर्म के सम्मान हेतु आयोजित हुई)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Harsha belonged to the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty of Thanesar (founded by Pushyabhuti / Prabhakaravardhana).
2. Harsha's sister Rajyashri was rescued from Malwa/Gauda ruler Shashanka (who cut down the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya).
3. Banabhatta was Harsha's court poet ('Harshacharita' and 'Kadambari').
qe: During Harshavardhana's reign (606–647 CE), what was the famous Buddhist assembly held at Kannauj (643 CE) presided over by Xuanzang primarily meant to honour?

q: विश्व प्रसिद्ध अजंता की शैलकृत बौद्ध गुफा चित्रकारी (महाराष्ट्र) को मुख्यतः गुप्तों के समकालीन किस दक्कन राजवंश का संरक्षण प्राप्त था?
e:
Vakataka rulers (notably Harishena, married into the Gupta family via Prabhavatigupta, daughter of Chandragupta II) patronized the finest Ajanta caves (Caves 16, 17, 19 — Jataka tales & Padmapani Bodhisattva) (अजंता की गुफाओं को मुख्यतः वाकाटक वंश का संरक्षण मिला)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Ajanta has 29–30 exclusively Buddhist caves; Ellora has 34 caves representing all three traditions—Buddhist (1–12), Hindu (13–29), and Jain (30–34).
2. Elephanta Caves (near Mumbai, famous for Trimurti Shiva) were patronized by the Kalachuris / Rashtrakutas.
3. Bagh Caves (Madhya Pradesh) also preserve Gupta-period mural paintings.
qe: The world-famous rock-cut Buddhist cave paintings of Ajanta (Maharashtra) were predominantly patronized by which Deccan dynasty contemporary to the Guptas?

q: महाबलीपुरम (ममल्लापुरम, तमिलनाडु) में प्रसिद्ध एकाश्म 'पंच रथ' और शोर मंदिर का निर्माण किस राजवंश ने कराया था?
e:
Pallava kings—especially Narasimhavarman I ('Mamalla', 630–668 CE) who built the Pancha Rathas and Narasimhavarman II ('Rajasimha') who built the Shore Temple & Kailasanatha Temple (Kanchipuram)—pioneered Dravida temple architecture (पल्लव शासकों ने महाबलीपुरम के रथ मंदिर बनवाए)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Mahendravarman I (Pallava) authored the satirical Sanskrit play 'Mattavilasa Prahasana'.
2. Dandin (author of 'Dashakumaracharita') lived at the Pallava court in Kanchipuram.
3. Kanchipuram (capital of Pallavas) was one of ancient India's seven sacred cities (Sapta Puri).
qe: The famous monolithic rock-cut 'Pancha Rathas' (Seven Pagodas) and Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram, Tamil Nadu) were built by which dynasty?

q: चोल शासक परान्तक प्रथम का 'उत्तरमेरुर अभिलेख' (10वीं शताब्दी ई.) ऐतिहासिक रूप से किसके विस्तृत नियमों के लिए प्रसिद्ध है?
o: Village assembly (Sabha) committee elections via 'Kudavolai' (lottery) system
e:
The Uttaramerur inscription specifies eligibility criteria (property, education, moral integrity, audit of past accounts) and the 'Kudavolai' (palm-leaf pot-ticket lottery) system for selecting village committees ('Variyams') (उत्तरमेरुर अभिलेख चोल ग्राम सभा के चुनाव नियमों से संबंधित है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Chola empire divisions (largest to smallest): Mandalams (provinces) → Valanadus → Nadus → Kurrams/Villages.
2. 'Ur' was the general village assembly; 'Sabha' was the assembly of Brahmin-grant villages (Agraharas); 'Nagaram' was the merchant guild assembly.
3. Famous Chola land tax was 'Kadamai'; 'Vetti' was forced labour.
qe: The 'Uttaramerur Inscription' (10th century CE) of Chola king Parantaka I is historically celebrated for providing detailed constitutional rules for:
oe: Village assembly (Sabha) committee elections via 'Kudavolai' (lottery) system

q: ओडिशा के कोणार्क स्थित प्रसिद्ध सूर्य मंदिर ('ब्लैक पैगोडा', 13वीं शताब्दी ई.), जिसे सूर्य के 24 पहियों वाले विशाल रथ के रूप में बनाया गया है, का निर्माण किसने कराया था?
e:
Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I built the Konark Sun Temple (~1250 CE) in Kalinga (Nagara) style (पूर्वी गंग शासक नरसिंहदेव प्रथम ने कोणार्क सूर्य मंदिर बनवाया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Anantavarman Chodaganga built the Jagannath Temple at Puri ('White Pagoda').
2. Lingaraja Temple at Bhubaneswar was built by Somavamshi rulers (Yayati Kesari).
3. Dilwara Jain Temples at Mount Abu (white marble, Solanki style) were built by Vimal Shah (1031) and Tejpala/Vastupala (1230).
qe: Who built the renowned Sun Temple at Konark ('Black Pagoda', Odisha, 13th century CE), designed as a colossal 24-wheeled chariot of Surya?

q: किस गुर्जर-प्रतिहार शासक—जिसकी प्रशंसा अरब यात्री सुलेमान ने भारत की सर्वश्रेष्ठ घुड़सवार सेना वाले 'जुज्र राजा' के रूप में की—ने 'आदिवराह' की उपाधि धारण की थी?
e:
Mihira Bhoja (836–885 CE, capital Kannauj) was the greatest Gurjara-Pratihara emperor, a devout Vaishnava who issued 'Adivaraha' dramma coins (मिहिर भोज ने आदिवराह की उपाधि धारण की)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Famous Sanskrit dramatist Rajashekhara ('Karpuramanjari', 'Kavyamimamsa') adorned the court of Mahendrapala I and Mahipala I.
2. Nagabhata I founded the Pratihara power and successfully repelled early Arab invasions from Sindh.
3. In 712 CE, Arab commander Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh (defeating Raja Dahir at the Battle of Rewar).
qe: Which Gurjara-Pratihara ruler—praised by Arab traveller Sulaiman as 'King Juzr' with the finest cavalry in India—was the greatest emperor of the dynasty and assumed the title 'Adivaraha'?

q: 'तूती-ए-हिन्द' (हिन्दुस्तान का तोता) के नाम से विख्यात किस प्रसिद्ध कवि, संगीतकार और इतिहासकार ने सात दिल्ली सुल्तानों का शासन देखा तथा कव्वाली व खड़ी बोली की नींव रखी?
e:
Amir Khusrau (born 1253 at Patiyali, Kasganj district, UP) served from Balban to Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq and authored 'Khazain-ul-Futuh', 'Tughlaqnama', and 'Nuh Sipihr' (अमीर खुसरो को तूती-ए-हिन्द कहा जाता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Ziauddin Barani authored 'Tarikh-i-Firozshahi' and 'Fatwa-i-Jahandari'.
2. Minhaj-us-Siraj authored 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri' (dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud).
3. Hasan Nizami wrote 'Taj-ul-Maasir' (first official history of the Delhi Sultanate).
qe: Which famous poet, musician, and historian—known as 'Tuti-i-Hind' (Parrot of India)—witnessed the reigns of seven Delhi Sultans and pioneered Qawwali, Sitar, and Khari Boli Hindi?

q: किस दिल्ली सुल्तान ने सिजदा और पैबोस की फारसी दरबारी प्रथाएँ शुरू कीं और 'जिल्ल-ए-इलाही' (ईश्वर की छाया) के दैवी राजत्व सिद्धांत का प्रतिपादन किया?
e:
Balban (1266–1287) elevated royal prestige through 'Niyabat-i-Khudai' (Vicegerent of God), 'Zill-i-Ilahi', Sijda, Paibos, and the Persian festival of Nauroz (बलबन ने सिजदा, पैबोस और जिल्ल-ए-इलाही का सिद्धांत लागू किया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Balban also created 'Diwan-i-Ariz' (separate military department) to counter Mongol invasions along the NW frontier.
2. Shah Jahan later abolished Sijda and replaced it with 'Chahar Taslim'.
3. The five dynasties of Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526): Slave (Mamluk) → Khalji → Tughlaq → Sayyid → Lodi (Tughlaqs ruled longest: 94 years; Khaljis shortest: 30 years).
qe: Which Delhi Sultan introduced the 'Persian' court customs of Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the Sultan's feet) and propounded the theory of Divine Kingship ('Zill-i-Ilahi' — Shadow of God)?

q: दिल्ली सल्तनत की भू-राजस्व व्यवस्था में मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक द्वारा प्रारंभ 'सोंधर' (या तकावी) क्या था?
o: A punitive tax levied on rebellious Zamindars
A religious levy on urban artisans
A toll tax collected on Silk Route caravans
Agricultural credit/loans advanced to peasants for buying seeds, bullocks, and digging wells
e:
Muhammad bin Tughlaq established 'Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi' (agriculture department) and distributed 'Sondhar' (Taqavi) loans to distressed peasants in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab to expand cultivation (सोंधर/तकावी किसानों को दिया जाने वाला कृषि ऋण था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Alauddin Khalji levied 'Ghari' (house tax) and 'Charai' (pasture/grazing tax) alongside 50% Kharaj land revenue.
2. In the Iqta system, an 'Iqtadar' (Muqti/Wali) collected revenue, maintained troops, and remitted surplus ('Fawazil') to the central treasury.
3. Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta visited Delhi in 1333 CE during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign.
qe: In the Delhi Sultanate land-revenue system, what was 'Sondhar' (or Taqavi) introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
oe: A punitive tax levied on rebellious Zamindars
A religious levy on urban artisans
A toll tax collected on Silk Route caravans
Agricultural credit/loans advanced to peasants for buying seeds, bullocks, and digging wells

q: किस लोदी शासक ने 1504 ई. में आगरा नगर की स्थापना की और 1506 ई. में इसे अपनी राजधानी बनाया?
e:
Sikandar Lodi (1489–1517, ablest Lodi ruler) founded Agra (1504), introduced 'Gaj-i-Sikandari', and composed Persian verses under the pen name 'Gulrukhi' (सिकन्दर लोदी ने 1504 में आगरा बसाया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Bahlul Lodi (1451) founded the Lodi dynasty—the first Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi.
2. Khizr Khan (1414) founded the Sayyid dynasty after Timur's devastating invasion of Delhi (1398).
3. During Sikandar Lodi's reign, the Ayurvedic treatise 'Farhang-i-Sikandari' (Tibb-i-Sikandari) and music work 'Lahjat-i-Sikandarshahi' were compiled.
qe: Which Lodi ruler founded the city of Agra in 1504 CE and made it his capital in 1506 CE to control the Rajput chiefs of Rajasthan and Malwa?

q: दिल्ली की 'कुव्वत-उल-इस्लाम मस्जिद' और अजमेर के 'अढ़ाई दिन का झोंपड़ा' का निर्माण दिल्ली सल्तनत के किस संस्थापक ने कराया था?
e:
Qutb-ud-din Aibak built Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque (Delhi, 1193), Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra (Ajmer), and laid the foundation of Qutub Minar; he died in 1210 at Lahore while playing Chaugan (polo) (कुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक ने इन दोनों स्मारकों का निर्माण कराया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Iltutmish completed the Qutub Minar (up to 4th storey); Firoz Shah Tughlaq later rebuilt the damaged top and added the 5th storey.
2. Alauddin Khalji built 'Alai Darwaza'—featuring the first true scientific dome and horseshoe arch in Indo-Islamic architecture.
3. The tomb of Balban in Mehrauli (Delhi) contains the first true arch in India.
qe: The 'Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque' (Delhi) and 'Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra' (Ajmer) were constructed by which founder of the Delhi Sultanate?

q: महाराष्ट्र के किस भक्ति संत ने पंढरपुर के भगवान विट्ठल को समर्पित 'अभंग' रचे और जिनके पद गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में भी संकलित हैं?
e:
Sant Namdev (1270–1350, Varkari tradition) travelled widely to North India and 61 of his devotional hymns are preserved in the Sikh scripture Guru Granth Sahib (संत नामदेव के पद गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में संकलित हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Sant Jnaneswar (Dnyaneshwar) wrote 'Jnaneswari' (Marathi commentary on Bhagavad Gita) in 1290 CE.
2. Sant Tukaram was a contemporary of Shivaji; Samarth Ramdas ('Dasbodh') was Shivaji's spiritual preceptor.
3. Sankaradeva (Assam) founded 'Ekasarana Dharma' and Sattriya classical dance/Bhaona theatre.
qe: Which Bhakti saint from Maharashtra composed devotional 'Abhangas' dedicated to Lord Vitthala of Pandharpur and whose hymns are included in the Guru Granth Sahib?

q: सिख धर्म के संस्थापक कौन थे, जिनका जन्म 1469 ई. में तलवंडी (ननकाना साहिब) में हुआ और जिन्होंने 'इक ओंकार' व 'लंगर' परंपरा शुरू की?
e:
Guru Nanak Dev (1469–1539, contemporary of Babur) founded Sikhism, emphasizing Naam Japna, Kirat Karna, and Vand Chhakna (गुरु नानक देव सिख धर्म के संस्थापक थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Guru Angad (2nd Guru) standardized the Gurmukhi script; Guru Ram Das (4th) founded Amritsar; Guru Arjan Dev (5th) compiled the Adi Granth (1604) and built Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple).
2. Guru Tegh Bahadur (9th Guru) was martyred in Delhi under Aurangzeb (1675).
3. Guru Gobind Singh (10th Guru) founded the Khalsa Panth on Baisakhi 1699 at Anandpur Sahib.
qe: Who was the founder of Sikhism, born in 1469 CE at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib), who preached 'Ik Onkar' (One God) and institutionalized 'Langar' (community kitchen)?

q: 23 जनवरी 1565 को चार दक्कन सल्तनतों (बीजापुर, अहमदनगर, गोलकुंडा, बीदर) की संयुक्त सेना और विजयनगर के रामराय के बीच लड़ा गया कौन-सा निर्णायक युद्ध हम्पी के पतन का कारण बना?
e:
In the Battle of Talikota (Bannihatti / Rakshasi-Tangadi, 1565), the Deccan coalition defeated Aliya Rama Raya (regent of Sadashiva Raya); Berar was the ONLY Deccan Sultanate that did NOT join the coalition (तालीकोटा युद्ध 1565 में बरार शामिल नहीं था)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. After Talikota, the Aravidu dynasty shifted the Vijayanagara capital to Penukonda and later Chandragiri.
2. Gol Gumbaz (Bijapur, world's second largest unsupported dome with whispering gallery) was built by Muhammad Adil Shah.
3. Charminar (Hyderabad, 1591) was built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda.
qe: Which decisive battle fought on 23 January 1565 between the combined armies of the four Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar) and Rama Raya of Vijayanagara led to the sack of Hampi?

q: दक्षिण भारतीय भक्ति परंपरा में 'अलवार' तमिल संत-कवि किस देवता के उपासक थे, जबकि 'नयनार' किस देवता के उपासक थे?
e:
The 12 Alvars were Vaishnava saints (hymns compiled in 'Nalayira Divya Prabandham'; Andal was the only female Alvar), and the 63 Nayanars were Shaiva saints (Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar, Karaikkal Ammaiyar) (अलवार विष्णु भक्त और नयनार शिव भक्त थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Ramananda (14th–15th century, Varanasi) bridged South Indian Bhakti to North India; his 12 disciples included Kabir, Ravidas, Sena, Dhanna, and Pipa.
2. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (Bengal) popularized Gaudiya Vaishnavism and Sankirtana (Achintya Bhedabheda).
3. Mirabai (Merta, Rajasthan) and Surdas (Braj) were foremost Saguna Krishna-bhakti poets of North India.
qe: In South Indian Bhakti traditions, the 'Alvars' were Tamil poet-saints devoted to which deity, whereas the 'Nayanars' were devoted to which deity?

q: किस मुगल सम्राट के शासनकाल (1628–1658) को 'मुगल स्थापत्य का स्वर्ण युग' कहा जाता है, जिसमें ताजमहल, लाल किला (दिल्ली) और जामा मस्जिद का निर्माण हुआ?
e:
Shah Jahan's reign saw the pinnacle of white marble architecture, Pietra Dura floral inlay, and the Peacock Throne (Takht-i-Taus, built by Bebadal Khan) (शाहजहाँ का काल मुगल स्थापत्य का स्वर्ण युग कहलाता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Ustad Ahmad Lahori was the chief architect of the Taj Mahal (built 1632–1653 in memory of Mumtaz Mahal).
2. Shah Jahan shifted the Mughal capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad (Old Delhi) in 1638–48.
3. Humayun's Tomb (Delhi, built by Haji Begum, architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas) introduced the double dome and Charbagh garden style in India.
qe: Which Mughal emperor's reign (1628–1658) is celebrated as the 'Golden Age of Mughal Architecture', witnessing the construction of the Taj Mahal, Red Fort (Delhi), and Jama Masjid?

q: इंग्लैंड के सम्राट जेम्स प्रथम का वह कौन-सा राजदूत था जो सम्राट जहाँगीर के दरबार (1615–1619) में रहा और अंग्रेजों के लिए व्यापारिक फरमान प्राप्त किया?
e:
Sir Thomas Roe arrived at Ajmer in 1615 as official ambassador of King James I to Jahangir and obtained trading privileges across the Mughal Empire (सर थॉमस रो 1615 में जहाँगीर के दरबार में आए)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Captain William Hawkins had visited Jahangir earlier (1608–11); Jahangir called him 'English Khan' and granted him a 400 mansab.
2. French diamond merchant Tavernier and physician Francois Bernier visited India during Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb's reigns.
3. Jahangir installed the famous 'Chain of Justice' (Zanjir-i-Adl) at Agra Fort and wrote 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri' in Persian.
qe: Who was the English East India Company envoy sent by King James I who stayed at Emperor Jahangir's court (1615–1619) and secured trade farmans for English factories?

q: प्रसिद्ध हल्दीघाटी का युद्ध (18 जून 1576) मेवाड़ के महाराणा प्रताप और किसके नेतृत्व वाली मुगल सेना के बीच लड़ा गया था?
e:
Raja Man Singh (assisted by Asaf Khan) led Akbar's imperial army against Maharana Pratap (supported by Hakim Khan Sur and Bhil archers led by Rana Punja) at Haldighati (हल्दीघाटी युद्ध में मुगल सेना का नेतृत्व राजा मानसिंह ने किया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Second Battle of Panipat (5 November 1556): Bairam Khan (for young Akbar) defeated Hemu (Hemchandra Vikramaditya).
2. Tansen (Ramtanu Pandey, born in Gwalior) was the legendary classical musician among Akbar's Navaratnas.
3. Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana translated Baburnama from Turki into Persian.
qe: The famous Battle of Haldighati (18 June 1576) was fought between Maharana Pratap of Mewar and the Mughal army commanded by:

q: किस मराठा पेशवा (1720–1740) ने, जो अजेय घुड़सवार रणनीतिकार और 'हिंदू पद पादशाही' के प्रवर्तक थे, मालवा, गुजरात और बुंदेलखंड होते हुए दिल्ली तक मराठा प्रभुत्व फैलाया?
e:
Peshwa Baji Rao I (son of Balaji Vishwanath) famously declared 'Let us strike at the trunk of the withering tree (Mughal Empire), and the branches will fall of themselves' and won ~40 undefeated battles including Palkhed (1728) against the Nizam (बाजीराव प्रथम ने मराठा शक्ति को दिल्ली तक फैलाया)।
Exam Booster Facts:

3. Treaty of Bassein (1802) was signed by Peshwa Baji Rao II accepting Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance, triggering the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
qe: Which Maratha Peshwa (1720–1740), famed as an undefeated cavalry strategist and proponent of 'Hindu Pad Padshahi', expanded Maratha supremacy across Malwa, Gujarat, and Bundelkhand up to Delhi?

q: अकबर की राजस्व प्रणाली के अंतर्गत मुगल भूमि वर्गीकरण में 'पोलज' (Polaj) भूमि किसे कहा जाता था?
o: Tax-free charitable land granted to scholars
Uncultivated wasteland for 5 or more years
Land cultivated continuously every year without ever being left fallow
e:
Todar Mal classified agricultural land into four categories: Polaj (cultivated annually — highest revenue), Parauti (left fallow 1–2 years), Chachar (fallow 3–4 years), and Banjar (uncultivated for 5+ years) (पोलज प्रतिवर्ष बोई जाने वाली सर्वाधिक उपजाऊ भूमि थी)।
Exam Booster Facts:

2. Mughal empire was divided into Subas (provinces) → Sarkars (districts) → Parganas (sub-districts) → Mauzas/Villages.
3. Subedar (Sipahsalar) was the provincial governor, while Diwan handled provincial finances independently as a check on the Subedar.
qe: In Mughal land classification under Akbar's revenue system, what was 'Polaj' land?
oe: Tax-free charitable land granted to scholars
Uncultivated wasteland for 5 or more years
Land cultivated continuously every year without ever being left fallow

q: भारत के किस गवर्नर-जनरल ने राजा राममोहन राय के सक्रिय सहयोग से 1829 का विनियम XVII पारित कर सती प्रथा का उन्मूलन किया?
e:
Lord William Bentinck (first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833) abolished Sati in December 1829 and suppressed Thuggee through Colonel William Sleeman (लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिंक ने 1829 में सती प्रथा समाप्त की)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Bentinck also adopted Macaulay's Minute on English Education (1835).
2. Lord Ellenborough abolished slavery in India via Act V of 1843.
3. Lord Canning was the last Governor-General of the Company and first Viceroy of India (1858).
qe: Which Governor-General of India enacted Regulation XVII of 1829 abolishing the cruel practice of Sati with the active support of Raja Ram Mohan Roy?

q: 1773 के रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट ने बंगाल के गवर्नर-जनरल (वॉरेन हेस्टिंग्स) का पद सृजित किया और 1774 में किस शहर में एक सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की स्थापना की?
e:
The Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta was established in 1774 with Sir Elijah Impey as its first Chief Justice and 3 puisne judges (1774 में कलकत्ता में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय स्थापित हुआ)।
Exam Booster Facts:

q: भारत सरकार के आधिकारिक शताब्दी इतिहास ग्रन्थ 'एटीन फिफ्टी-सेवन' (1957) के लेखक कौन थे, जबकि वी. डी. सावरकर ने 1857 को 'भारत का प्रथम स्वतंत्रता संग्राम' कहा था?

Dr. Surendra Nath Sen authored the official centenary history 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven' (1957) (एस. एन. सेन ने 'एटीन फिफ्टी-सेवन' लिखा)।

q: लॉर्ड कर्जन ने बंगाल का विभाजन किस वर्ष लागू किया, जिसने पूरे भारत में स्वदेशी और बहिष्कार आंदोलन को जन्म दिया?
e:
Partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905 (observed as Raksha Bandhan & National Mourning Day); it was annulled at the Delhi Durbar in December 1911 under Lord Hardinge II, when the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi (16 अक्टूबर 1905 को बंगाल विभाजन लागू हुआ)।
Exam Booster Facts:

qe: In which year did Lord Curzon execute the Partition of Bengal, sparking the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement across India?

q: जलियाँवाला बाग हत्याकांड (13 अप्रैल 1919, अमृतसर) किस दमनकारी कानून ('न दलील, न वकील, न अपील') के विरोध प्रदर्शनों के दौरान हुआ था?
o: Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919)
e:
People gathered at Jallianwala Bagh on Baisakhi (13 April 1919) to protest the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal; Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered indiscriminate firing (रॉलेट एक्ट के विरोध में जलियाँवाला बाग सभा हुई थी)।
Exam Booster Facts:

qe: The tragic Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (13 April 1919, Amritsar) occurred during protests against which repressive legislation ('No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal')?
oe: Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919)

q: 'सर्वेंट्स ऑफ इंडिया सोसाइटी' (1905) के संस्थापक कौन थे और जिन्हें महात्मा गांधी अपना राजनीतिक गुरु मानते थे?
e:
Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune (1905), presided over the 1905 Banaras INC session, and mentored Mahatma Gandhi upon his return from South Africa in 1915 (गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले गांधीजी के राजनीतिक गुरु थे)।

q: सौरमंडल का कौन-सा ग्रह 'भोर का तारा' और 'सांझ का तारा' कहलाता है तथा पूर्व से पश्चिम की ओर (प्रतिगामी घूर्णन) घूमता है?
e:
Venus (brightest and hottest planet due to dense CO₂ runaway greenhouse effect) and Uranus rotate clockwise (East to West), opposite to all other planets (शुक्र पूर्व से पश्चिम घूमता है और भोर/सांझ का तारा कहलाता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:

2. Jupiter is the largest planet; Saturn has the lowest density (less than water) and prominent rings.

qe: Which planet in the Solar System is known as the 'Morning Star' and 'Evening Star' and rotates from East to West (retrograde rotation)?

q: वर्ष की किन दो तिथियों को विषुव (Equinox — संपूर्ण पृथ्वी पर दिन और रात बराबर, सूर्य भूमध्य रेखा पर लंबवत) होता है?
e:
Vernal Equinox occurs around 21 March and Autumnal Equinox around 23 September (21 मार्च और 23 सितंबर को विषुव होता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Summer Solstice (21 June): Sun overhead at Tropic of Cancer (longest day in Northern Hemisphere); Winter Solstice (22 December): Sun overhead at Tropic of Capricorn.
2. Perihelion (Earth closest to Sun, ~147 million km) occurs on 3 January; Aphelion (farthest, ~152 million km) occurs on 4 July.
3. Earth's axial tilt of 23.5° (66.5° to the orbital plane) causes the change of seasons.
qe: On which two dates of the year do Equinoxes (विषुव — equal day and night all over the Earth, Sun vertically overhead at the Equator) occur?

q: पृथ्वी की भूपर्पटी के भीतर वह बिंदु जहाँ भूकंप उत्पन्न होता है क्या कहलाता है, तथा इसके ठीक ऊपर पृथ्वी की सतह पर स्थित बिंदु को क्या कहते हैं?
e:
Focus (Hypocentre) is the underground origin of seismic energy, while Epicentre is the point directly above it on the surface where seismic waves arrive first (उत्पत्ति बिंदु भूकंप मूल/फोकस तथा सतही बिंदु अधिकेंद्र/एपीसेंटर कहलाता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Isoseismal lines join places experiencing equal earthquake intensity; Homoseismal lines join places experiencing seismic waves at the exact same time.
2. Deep-focus earthquakes (>300 km) occur mainly along Benioff–Wadati subduction zones at convergent plate boundaries.
3. India is divided into four seismic zones (Zones II, III, IV, and V — Zone V being the highest risk, covering Himalayas, NE India, Kutch, Andaman & Nicobar).
qe: Which term describes the point inside the Earth's crust where an earthquake originates, and what is the point on the Earth's surface directly above it called?

q: 'डोलड्रम्स' (शांत पेटी) — शांत पवनों और दोपहर की संवहनीय वर्षा वाली विषुवतरेखीय निम्न दाब पेटी — को अन्य किस नाम से जाना जाता है?
e:
The Doldrums (5° N to 5° S) correspond to the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) where Northeast and Southeast Trade Winds converge and rise (डोलड्रम्स को अंतःउष्णकटिबंधीय अभिसरण क्षेत्र — ITCZ — भी कहा जाता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. 'Horse Latitudes' (अश्व अक्षांश) refer to the Sub-Tropical High-Pressure Belts around 30°–35° N and S, characterized by subsiding dry air and world's major hot deserts.
2. Convectional rainfall occurs almost daily at ~4 PM ('4 o'clock rain') in equatorial regions.
3. Planetary wind systems: Trade Winds (Easterlies), Westerlies, and Polar Easterlies.
qe: The 'Doldrums' (शांत पेटी) — a low-pressure equatorial belt of calm winds and frequent afternoon convectional thunderstorms — is also known as:

q: किस प्रकार के बादल सघन, ऊँचे ऊर्ध्वाधर बादल होते हैं जो भारी गरज-चमक, बिजली और ओलावृष्टि के लिए उत्तरदायी होते हैं?
e:
Cumulonimbus clouds have anvil-shaped tops and produce violent thunderstorms, torrential rain, and hail (कपासी वर्षी मेघ गरज-चमक व ओलावृष्टि के लिए उत्तरदायी हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Cirrus clouds are the highest feathery ice-crystal clouds (~8–12 km), indicating fair weather or an approaching warm front.
2. Nimbostratus clouds are dark grey low-level layers producing continuous steady rain.
3. Halo around the Sun or Moon is typically formed by refraction through Cirrostratus clouds.
qe: Which type of clouds are dense, towering vertical clouds extending from low to high altitudes, responsible for heavy thunderstorms, lightning, and hailstorms?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी स्थलाकृति समुद्री तरंगों द्वारा निर्मित एक 'अपरदनात्मक' (erosional) स्थलाकृति है, न कि निक्षेपात्मक?
e:
Sea Cliffs, Wave-cut Platforms, Sea Caves, Sea Arches, and Sea Stacks are coastal EROSIONAL landforms; Beaches, Spits, Bars, and Tombolos are DEPOSITIONAL landforms (समुद्री स्टैक व मेहराब अपरदनात्मक स्थलाकृतियाँ हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Glacial erosional landforms: Cirque (Corrie), Arete, Horn (Matterhorn), U-shaped valley, Hanging valley, Fjord.
2. Glacial depositional landforms: Moraines, Drumlins ('Basket of Eggs' topography), Eskers, Outwash plains.
3. Fluvial erosional landforms: V-shaped valley, Gorge, Canyon, Waterfall, Pot-holes; depositional: Alluvial fan, Delta, Floodplain.
qe: Which of the following landforms is an EROSIONAL landform carved by sea waves (coastal geomorphic agent) rather than a depositional landform?

q: शुष्क पृथ्वी के वायुमंडल के आयतन का लगभग 78% भाग किस गैस से बना है?
e:
Dry air consists of ~78.08% Nitrogen, ~20.95% Oxygen, ~0.93% Argon, and ~0.04% Carbon dioxide (नाइट्रोजन लगभग 78% है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Argon is the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere (most abundant inert/noble gas).
2. Water vapour varies from 0% (deserts/poles) to ~4% (humid tropics) and absorbs terrestrial infrared radiation.
3. Dust particles (aerosols) act as hygroscopic nuclei essential for condensation and cloud formation.
qe: Which gas makes up approximately 78% of the dry Earth's atmosphere by volume?

q: जलवायु विज्ञान में 'एल्बिडो' (Albedo) क्या है, और किस प्राकृतिक पृथ्वी सतह का एल्बिडो सर्वाधिक होता है?
o: Percentage of incoming solar radiation absorbed by oceans; Deep ocean water
Fraction/percentage of incoming solar radiation reflected back by a surface; Fresh snow
Heat trapped by urban concrete; Asphalt roads
Rate of terrestrial long-wave radiation; Tropical rainforest
e:
Albedo is the reflectivity of a surface (ratio of reflected to incident solar radiation). Earth's average albedo is ~30%–35%; Fresh Snow has the highest natural albedo (~80%–90%), while dark oceans/asphalt have very low albedo (<10%) (ताजी बर्फ का एल्बिडो सर्वाधिक 80–90% होता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Melting of Arctic sea ice reduces albedo, causing more solar absorption and accelerating warming ('Ice-Albedo Feedback').
2. Insolation (Incoming Solar Radiation) is measured by a Pyranometer.
3. Heat Budget of Earth maintains long-term thermal equilibrium (~65 units absorbed = 65 units radiated back as long-wave terrestrial radiation).
qe: What is 'Albedo' (एल्बिडो) in climatology, and which natural Earth surface has the highest albedo?
oe: Percentage of incoming solar radiation absorbed by oceans; Deep ocean water
Fraction/percentage of incoming solar radiation reflected back by a surface; Fresh snow
Heat trapped by urban concrete; Asphalt roads
Rate of terrestrial long-wave radiation; Tropical rainforest

q: 'सारगैसो सागर', जो विश्व का एकमात्र बिना किसी स्थलीय सीमा वाला सागर है (केवल महासागरीय धाराओं से घिरा), किस महासागर में स्थित है?
e:
The Sargasso Sea lies in the North Atlantic subtropical gyre, enclosed by the Gulf Stream (west), North Atlantic Drift (north), Canary Current (east), and North Equatorial Current (south) (सारगैसो सागर उत्तरी अटलांटिक महासागर में स्थित है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. It has very high salinity (~37‰) and calm, clear blue waters.
2. The Bermuda Triangle lies along the western edge of the Sargasso Sea.
3. Oceanic oozes (pelagic deposits) include calcareous Globigerina ooze and siliceous Radiolarian/Diatom ooze.
qe: The 'Sargasso Sea', famous as the only sea in the world without any land boundaries (bounded solely by ocean currents and covered with floating Sargassum seaweed), is located in which ocean?

q: प्रवाल भित्ति निर्माण के 'अवतलन सिद्धांत' (तटीय प्रवाल भित्ति → अवरोधक प्रवाल भित्ति → एटॉल) को 1842 में किस प्रकृतिवादी ने प्रस्तुत किया था?
e:
Charles Darwin proposed the Subsidence Theory (1842) after his HMS Beagle voyage; Reginald Daly proposed the Glacial Control Theory (1915), and John Murray proposed the Standstill Theory (चार्ल्स डार्विन ने अवतलन सिद्धांत दिया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Great Barrier Reef (off Queensland, Australia) is the world's largest coral reef system.
2. Corals thrive in clear, shallow (<50 m), warm (20°–25°C), saline (27–30‰) tropical waters in symbiosis with Zooxanthellae algae.
3. Rising sea temperatures cause 'Coral Bleaching' (expulsion of Zooxanthellae).
qe: According to the 'Subsidence Theory' of coral reef formation (Fringing Reef → Barrier Reef → Atoll), which naturalist proposed this classic evolutionary sequence in 1842?

q: मृदा वर्गीकरण में यूक्रेन/रूसी स्टेपी और उत्तरी अमेरिकी प्रेयरी की गहरी, ह्यूमस-युक्त अत्यधिक उपजाऊ 'काली मिट्टी' (Black Earth) को क्या कहा जाता है?
e:
Chernozem ('Black Earth', Mollisols in USDA) is the world's most fertile zonal soil, ideal for large-scale wheat cultivation in Ukraine, Russia, and US/Canadian Prairies (चर्नोजेम विश्व की सर्वाधिक उपजाऊ मृदा है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Podzol is an acidic, ash-grey leached soil of cool coniferous Taiga forests.
2. V. V. Dokuchaev (Russia) is revered as the 'Father of Modern Soil Science' (Pedology).
3. Laterite forms under intense tropical leaching (high heat + heavy rain), leaving iron and aluminium oxides.
qe: Which soil order in the USDA / Russian zonal soil classification is the dark, humus-rich, ultra-fertile 'Black Earth' of the Ukraine/Russian Steppe and North American Prairies?

q: 'भ्रंश घाटी' (Rift Valley — जैसे पूर्वी अफ्रीकी भ्रंश घाटी और नर्मदा घाटी) मुख्यतः किस विवर्तनिक प्रक्रिया से बनती है?
e:
A Rift Valley (Graben) forms when tensional forces pull the crust apart and the central block drops down between two normal faults; the uplifted flanking blocks are called Horsts (Block Mountains) (तनावजनित भ्रंशन से भ्रंश घाटी बनती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Rhine Rift Valley (Europe) is flanked by Vosges (France) and Black Forest (Germany) block mountains.
2. Lake Tanganyika, Lake Malawi, and the Dead Sea lie inside the Afro-Arabian Rift system.
3. Fold mountains (Himalayas, Andes, Alps, Rockies) form by compressional tectonic forces at convergent boundaries.
qe: The 'Rift Valley' (भ्रंश घाटी) — such as the Great East African Rift Valley and the Narmada Valley — is formed primarily by which tectonic process?
oe: Tensional faulting where a central crustal block subsides between two parallel faults

q: ऊपरी क्षोभमंडल (9–12 किमी ऊँचाई) में बहने वाली संकीर्ण, तीव्र गति की विसर्पी पश्चिमी वायु धाराओं को क्या कहा जाता है, जो भारतीय मानसून और शीतकालीन पश्चिमी विक्षोभ को गहराई से प्रभावित करती हैं?
e:
Jet Streams (discovered during WWII high-altitude flights; named by Rossby) are geostrophic upper-air rivers of wind; the Tropical Easterly Jet (TEJ) aids summer monsoon bursts, while the Sub-Tropical Westerly Jet (STWJ) guides winter Western Disturbances into North India (जेट स्ट्रीम मानसून व पश्चिमी विक्षोभ को नियंत्रित करती हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Jet stream meanders are known as 'Rossby Waves'.
2. P. Koteswaram (Indian meteorologist) established the crucial link between the Tibetan Plateau heating, Tropical Easterly Jet, and Indian Monsoon.
3. Sudden weakening of the Polar Vortex/Jet Stream brings severe Arctic cold waves to mid-latitudes.
qe: What is the name of the narrow, high-speed, meandering westerly air currents blowing in the upper troposphere (9–12 km altitude) that strongly influence Indian monsoon onset and winter Western Disturbances?

q: मानव भूगोल की किस दार्शनिक विचारधारा का तर्क है कि प्रकृति केवल संभावनाएँ प्रस्तुत करती है और मानव अपनी बुद्धि व तकनीक से उनका चयन करता है (विडाल डी ला ब्लाश द्वारा प्रवर्तित)?
e:
Possibilism (संभववाद, French school led by Vidal de la Blache; term coined by Lucien Febvre) counters Environmental Determinism ("Nature is never more than an adviser") (संभववाद के जनक विडाल डी ला ब्लाश हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Determinism exponents: Friedrich Ratzel, Ellen Churchill Semple, Ellsworth Huntington.
2. Neo-Determinism ('Stop-and-Go' / Traffic Policeman analogy): Griffith Taylor.
3. Quantitative Revolution in geography emerged in the 1950s–60s (Fred Schaefer, Peter Haggett, Richard Chorley), followed by Humanistic Geography (Yi-Fu Tuan) and Welfare Geography (David Smith).
qe: Which philosophical school of Human Geography argues that while nature sets broad limits, human beings possess intelligence, technology, and free will to choose among various possibilities (founded by Paul Vidal de la Blache)?

q: किस प्रसिद्ध जर्मन भूगोलवेत्ता ने 'कॉसमॉस' (5 खण्डों में) की रचना की और जिन्हें कार्ल रिटर ('अर्डकुण्डे') के साथ आधुनिक भूगोल का सह-संस्थापक माना जाता है?
e:
Alexander von Humboldt (1769–1859) wrote 'Kosmos', drew the first Isotherm map, and studied the Peru (Humboldt) Current and altitudinal vegetation zonation in the Andes (हम्बोल्ट ने 'कॉसमॉस' लिखा)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Eratosthenes (Greek, ~276–194 BCE) coined the word 'Geography' and calculated Earth's circumference accurately.
2. Hecataeus ('Ges Periodos') is often called the 'Father of Geography' in ancient Greece; Strabo wrote 'Geographica' (17 volumes); Ptolemy wrote 'Almagest' & 'Geographia'.
3. Bernhard Varenius ('Geographia Generalis', 1650) initiated the dichotomy between General (Systematic) and Special (Regional) Geography.
qe: Which classical German geographer authored 'Kosmos' (5 volumes) and is celebrated as a co-founder of modern geography alongside Carl Ritter ('Erdkunde')?

q: ग्रिफिथ टेलर के मानव प्रजाति उद्भव के 'प्रवास कटिबंध सिद्धांत' (Migration Zone Theory) के अनुसार, कौन-सा प्रजातीय समूह सबसे पहले विकसित हुआ और बाहरी किनारों (जैसे ऑस्ट्रेलिया व दक्षिणी अफ्रीका) की ओर धकेल दिया गया?
e:
Griffith Taylor argued human races originated in Central Asia in successive waves—Negrito (oldest, pushed farthest out) → Negro → Australoid → Mediterranean → Nordic → Alpine (youngest, closest to Central Asian core) (नीग्रिटो सबसे प्राचीन प्रजाति है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. B. S. Guha (1931 Census) classified India's population into 6 main racial elements: Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid, Mediterranean, Western Brachycephals, and Nordic.
2. Sentinelese, Onge, Jarawa, and Great Andamanese of Andaman Islands belong to the Negrito stock.
3. Most tribal groups of Central India (Gond, Santhal, Bhil, Munda) belong predominantly to the Proto-Australoid stock.
qe: According to Griffith Taylor's 'Migration Zone Theory' (Zones and Strata Theory) of human racial evolution, which racial group evolved earliest and was pushed to the outermost peripheral margins (like Australia and Southern Africa)?

q: ई. डब्ल्यू. बर्गेस के नगरीय भूमि उपयोग के 'संकेंद्रित वलय मॉडल' (1925, शिकागो पर आधारित) में केंद्रीय व्यापार क्षेत्र (CBD / जोन 1) के ठीक चारों ओर कौन-सा क्षेत्र स्थित होता है?
o: संक्रमण क्षेत्र — कारखाने व मलिन बस्तियाँ
e:
Burgess's 5 concentric rings outward from centre: 1. CBD → 2. Zone in Transition (light manufacturing, deteriorating housing/slums) → 3. Zone of Independent Workingmen's Homes → 4. Zone of Better Residences → 5. Commuters' Zone (CBD के ठीक बाहर संक्रमण क्षेत्र होता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Homer Hoyt (1939) proposed the Sector Model (wedges expanding along transport routes).
2. C. D. Harris & E. L. Ullman (1945) proposed the Multiple Nuclei Model (cities grow around several specialized nodes).
3. Lewis Mumford classified cities into six evolutionary stages: Eopolis → Polis → Metropolis → Megalopolis → Tyrannopolis → Nekropolis.
qe: In E. W. Burgess's 'Concentric Zone Model' (1925, based on Chicago) of urban land use, which zone immediately surrounds the Central Business District (CBD / Zone 1)?

q: जनसंख्या के 'कायिक घनत्व' (Physiological Density) को निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सूत्र सही रूप से परिभाषित करता है?
e:
Physiological Density = Total Population ÷ Net Cultivated Area (measuring actual population pressure on arable land) (कुल जनसंख्या ÷ निवल कृषित क्षेत्रफल = कायिक घनत्व)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Arithmetic Density = Total Population ÷ Total Land Area.
2. Agricultural Density = Total Agricultural Population (cultivators + agricultural labourers) ÷ Net Cultivated Area.
3. Economic Density relates population to total available productive resources.
qe: Which formula correctly defines 'Physiological Density' (कायिक घनत्व) of population?

q: नीलगिरि पहाड़ियों (तमिलनाडु) की कौन-सी भारतीय जनजाति भैंस पालन, अर्ध-बेलनाकार झोपड़ियों और पारंपरिक बहुपति प्रथा के लिए प्रसिद्ध है?
e:
The Toda tribe of the Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu) are traditional buffalo pastoralists (टोडा जनजाति नीलगिरि की पहाड़ियों में निवास करती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. As per Census 2011, Bhil is the largest Scheduled Tribe in India, followed by Gond and Santhal.
2. Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia are matrilineal tribes of Meghalaya; Lepcha and Bhutia inhabit Sikkim; Changpa (pashmina goat herders) inhabit Ladakh.
3. Gaddi and Gujjar-Bakarwal practice 'Transhumance' (ऋतु प्रवास — seasonal movement between high alpine pastures in summer and valleys in winter) in Himachal Pradesh & J&K.
qe: Which Indian tribe of the Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu) is famous for pastoral buffalo herding, barrel-vaulted huts, and traditional polyandry?

q: जी. के. जिप के 'कोटि-आकार नियम' (Rank-Size Rule, 1949) के अनुसार, यदि किसी देश के सबसे बड़े (प्रथम रैंक) नगर की जनसंख्या 12 मिलियन है, तो तीसरे रैंक के नगर की अपेक्षित जनसंख्या कितनी होगी?
e:
By Zipf's Rank-Size Rule: Pₙ = P₁ ÷ n. For P₁ = 12 million and n = 3: P₃ = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 million (P₃ = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 मिलियन)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Mark Jefferson's 'Law of the Primate City' (1939) describes countries where the largest city is disproportionately dominant (e.g., Bangkok, Paris, London, Mexico City) rather than following Zipf's rule.
2. India does NOT have a single national primate city (due to multiple mega-cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Chennai).
3. Functional classification of Indian towns was pioneered by Ashok Mitra (1961 Census).
qe: According to G. K. Zipf's 'Rank-Size Rule' (कोटि-आकार नियम, 1949), if the largest (rank 1) city in a country has a population of 12 million, what is the expected population of the 3rd-ranked city?

q: हिंदी, संस्कृत, अंग्रेजी, फारसी और रूसी सभी किस विश्व भाषा परिवार (Language Family) से संबंधित हैं?
e:
The Indo-European (भारोपीय) family is the world's largest language family by speakers, covering ~73% of India's population (Indo-Aryan branch) (हिंदी, संस्कृत, अंग्रेजी, फारसी व रूसी भारोपीय परिवार की भाषाएँ हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. India's four main language families: Indo-Aryan (~73%), Dravidian (~20% — Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam), Austro-Asiatic/Munda (~1.3% — Santhali, Mundari, Khasi), and Sino-Tibetan/Kirata (~0.8%).
2. Sir William Jones (founder of Asiatic Society of Bengal, 1784) highlighted the common ancestry of Sanskrit, Greek, and Latin.
3. Mandarin Chinese (Sino-Tibetan) has the most native speakers globally.
qe: Which term describes the global language family to which Hindi, Sanskrit, English, Persian, and Russian all belong?

q: फ्रांस, इटली और स्पेन जैसे भूमध्यसागरीय देशों की विशिष्ट वाणिज्यिक कृषि 'विटिकल्चर' (Viticulture) किससे संबंधित है?
e:
Viticulture is the specialized cultivation of grapes (अंगूर की खेती); Mediterranean climate's warm sunny summers produce high-sugar grapes ideal for wine and raisins.
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Sericulture = Silk farming; Apiculture = Bee-keeping; Pisciculture = Fish farming; Floriculture = Flower cultivation; Olericulture = Vegetable farming.
2. Truck Farming (market gardening) refers to growing fresh vegetables/fruits for distant urban markets via overnight trucks.
3. Dairy farming is most intensively developed in Northwest Europe (Denmark, Netherlands), New Zealand, and the US Great Lakes belt.
qe: What is 'Viticulture' (विटिकल्चर), an iconic commercial agricultural specialty of Mediterranean countries like France, Italy, and Spain?

q: विश्व में कच्चे तेल (पेट्रोलियम) का सर्वाधिक प्रमाणित भंडार किस देश के पास है, तथा यूरेनियम का सर्वाधिक भंडार किस देश के पास है?
e:
Venezuela holds the largest proven crude oil reserves (~300+ billion barrels, Orinoco Belt, followed by Saudi Arabia), while Australia holds the largest Uranium reserves (though Kazakhstan is the #1 producer of Uranium) (वेनेजुएला में सर्वाधिक तेल भंडार व ऑस्ट्रेलिया में सर्वाधिक यूरेनियम भंडार है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, est. 1960 in Baghdad) is headquartered in Vienna, Austria.
2. USA, Saudi Arabia, and Russia are the top three crude oil PRODUCERS globally.
3. India's Thorium reserves (Monazite sands of Kerala/Odisha coasts) are among the largest in the world.
qe: Which country holds the world's largest proven reserves of Petroleum (Crude Oil) and which country holds the largest reserves of Uranium?

q: डर्वेंट व्हिटल्सी के 'विश्व कृषि प्रदेशों' के प्रसिद्ध वर्गीकरण (1936) में उन्होंने विश्व भर में कितने भिन्न कृषि प्रदेशों की पहचान की थी?
e:
D. Whittlesey (1936) classified world agriculture into 13 major regions based on five functional criteria: crop-livestock association, farming methods, capital/labour intensity, disposal of products, and farm structures (व्हिटल्सी ने विश्व को 13 कृषि प्रदेशों में बाँटा)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Examples of Whittlesey's regions: Nomadic Herding, Livestock Ranching, Shifting Cultivation, Intensive Subsistence Tillage (Rice-dominant & Non-rice), Commercial Grain Farming, Mediterranean Agriculture, Plantation Agriculture.
2. Plantation crops (Tea, Coffee, Rubber, Cocoa, Oil Palm, Sugarcane) are capital-intensive, monoculture, export-oriented estates in the tropics.
3. Extensive Commercial Grain Farming (highly mechanized, low yield/acre but very high yield/person) dominates Prairies, Steppes, Pampas, and Downs.
qe: In Derwent Whittlesey's classic classification of 'World Agricultural Regions' (1936), how many distinct agricultural regions did he identify across the globe?

q: कौन-सी प्रसिद्ध संकीर्ण समुद्री जलसंधि मलय प्रायद्वीप को सुमात्रा (इंडोनेशिया) से अलग करती है और हिंद महासागर को दक्षिण चीन सागर से जोड़ने वाला सबसे व्यस्त नौवहन मार्ग है?
e:
The Strait of Malacca connects the Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean) with the South China Sea (Pacific), carrying over a quarter of world seaborne trade (मलक्का जलसंधि हिंद महासागर व दक्षिण चीन सागर को जोड़ती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Strait of Hormuz connects Persian Gulf & Gulf of Oman (vital oil choke point).
2. Strait of Gibraltar ('Key to the Mediterranean') separates Spain (Europe) from Morocco (Africa).
3. Bering Strait separates Asia (Russia) from North America (Alaska, USA), with the International Date Line passing through it.
qe: Which famous narrow maritime strait separates the Malay Peninsula from Sumatra (Indonesia) and serves as the busiest shipping choke point connecting the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea?

q: विश्व में बॉक्साइट (एल्यूमीनियम का प्रमुख अयस्क) का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक देश कौन-सा है?
e:
Australia (Weipa, Gove mines) is the world's #1 producer of Bauxite (and also Iron Ore and Lithium) (ऑस्ट्रेलिया बॉक्साइट उत्पादन में विश्व में प्रथम है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Guinea (West Africa) holds the world's largest bauxite reserves.
2. In India, Odisha (Panchpatmali, Koraput) produces over 70% of India's bauxite.
3. Aluminium smelting requires huge amounts of cheap hydroelectricity, so smelters often locate near power plants (e.g., HINDALCO at Renukoot near Rihand Dam, UP).
qe: Which country is the world's largest producer and exporter of Bauxite (the primary ore of Aluminium)?

q: अमेरिका के कैलिफोर्निया की 'सिलिकॉन वैली' विश्व स्तर पर किसके लिए प्रसिद्ध है, और किस भारतीय शहर को 'भारत की सिलिकॉन वैली' कहा जाता है?
e:
Silicon Valley (Santa Clara Valley, California) is the global hub of IT, software, and semiconductors; Bengaluru (Karnataka) is known as the 'Silicon Valley of India' (बेंगलुरु को भारत की सिलिकॉन वैली कहा जाता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Chennai is nicknamed the 'Detroit of India' (automobiles); Surat is the 'Diamond City of India'.
2. 'Technopole' refers to planned high-tech industrial/R&D hubs combining universities, startups, and venture capital.
3. IT/software is a classic 'footloose' Quaternary sector industry.
qe: What is 'Silicon Valley' in California (USA) globally famous for, and which Indian city is correspondingly called the 'Silicon Valley of India'?

q: GATT (1947) के स्थान पर 1 जनवरी 1995 को मराकेश समझौते के तहत स्थापित कौन-सा अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार संगठन विश्व भर में बहुपक्षीय व्यापार नियमों का नियमन करता है?
e:
The World Trade Organization (WTO, HQ Geneva, Switzerland) replaced GATT on 1 January 1995 following the Uruguay Round (1986–94) (विश्व व्यापार संगठन की स्थापना 1 जनवरी 1995 को हुई, मुख्यालय जिनेवा में है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Key WTO agreements: TRIPS (Intellectual Property), TRIMS (Investment), AoA (Agriculture — Amber, Blue, Green Box subsidies), and GATS (Services).
2. EU (European Union), ASEAN, USMCA (formerly NAFTA), SAARC, and BRICS are prominent regional/plurilateral trade & economic blocs.
3. IMF and World Bank (IBRD) are the 'Bretton Woods Twins' established in 1944 (HQ: Washington, D.C.).
qe: Which international trade organization, established on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement to replace GATT (1947), regulates multilateral trade rules worldwide?

q: कौन-सा गैर-पारंपरिक (नवीकरणीय) ऊर्जा संसाधन पृथ्वी की भूपर्पटी के नीचे संचित प्राकृतिक भाप व गर्म जल (जैसे लद्दाख की पूगा घाटी व हिमाचल के मणिकरण) का उपयोग करता है?
e:
Geothermal Energy utilizes Earth's internal heat; Iceland generates a huge share of its heating/electricity from geothermal power, and India's premier geothermal sites are Puga & Chumathang (Ladakh), Manikaran (HP), and Tattapani (Chhattisgarh) (पूगा घाटी व मणिकरण भू-तापीय ऊर्जा के प्रमुख केंद्र हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. International Solar Alliance (ISA, launched 2015 by India & France) is headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana.
2. Bhadla Solar Park (Jodhpur, Rajasthan) is one of the world's largest solar power parks.
3. Muppandal (Tamil Nadu) and Jaisalmer (Rajasthan) are India's largest wind farm clusters.
qe: Which non-conventional (renewable) energy resource harnesses natural steam and hot water trapped beneath the Earth's crust (such as at Puga Valley in Ladakh and Manikaran in Himachal Pradesh)?

q: वेबर के औद्योगिक अवस्थिति ढाँचे में, एक उद्योग जिसका पदार्थ सूचकांक (Material Index) 1 से काफी अधिक होता है (जैसे चीनी मिल या ताँबा प्रगलन), उसे क्या कहा जाता है?
e:
When MI > 1, the raw material loses substantial weight during processing (gross/weight-losing material: e.g., sugarcane yields only ~10% sugar), so locating near the raw material source minimizes transport cost (MI > 1 होने पर उद्योग कच्चे माल के निकट स्थापित होता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. If MI = 1 (pure material like raw cotton/yarn), the industry can locate at raw material, market, or intermediate point.
2. If MI < 1 (weight-gaining using ubiquitous water, e.g., soft drinks/bottling/bakery), it is market-oriented.
3. Sugar mills in India are shifting gradually from North India (UP/Bihar) toward Peninsular India (Maharashtra/Karnataka) due to higher sucrose content and longer crushing seasons.
qe: In Weber's industrial location framework, an industry whose Material Index (MI = Weight of localized raw materials ÷ Weight of finished product) is significantly GREATER than 1 (such as sugar milling or copper smelting) is classified as:

q: ओडिशा में स्थित भारत (तथा एशिया) की सबसे बड़ी खारे पानी की लैगून झील कौन-सी है, जो प्रवासी पक्षियों और इरावदी डॉल्फिन के लिए प्रसिद्ध है?
e:
Chilika Lake (Odisha, south of Mahanadi delta) is India's largest brackish lagoon and was designated India's first Ramsar Wetland in 1981 (alongside Keoladeo NP) (चिल्का झील भारत की सबसे बड़ी खारे पानी की लैगून है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Vembanad Lake (Kerala) is India's longest lake (backwater / Kayal, hosts Nehru Trophy Boat Race).
2. Pulicat Lake straddles the Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu border (Sriharikota barrier island hosts ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre).
3. Loktak Lake (Manipur) is Northeast India's largest freshwater lake, famous for floating 'Phumdis'.
qe: Which is the largest brackish water lagoon in India (and Asia), located in Odisha and famous as a wintering ground for migratory birds and Irrawaddy dolphins?

q: निम्नलिखित में से किस प्रायद्वीपीय नदी को 'दक्षिण गंगा' कहा जाता है और जिसका अपवाह बेसिन प्रायद्वीपीय भारत में सबसे बड़ा है?
e:
Godavari (1,465 km, rises at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik, Maharashtra) is the longest peninsular river ('Dakshin Ganga' / 'Vridha Ganga') (गोदावरी को दक्षिण गंगा कहा जाता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Major tributaries of Godavari: Pranhita (Wardha + Wainganga + Penganga), Indravati, Manjra, Sabari.
2. Kaveri (rises at Talakaveri, Brahmagiri Hills, Karnataka) is perennial because its upper catchment gets SW monsoon and lower catchment gets NE monsoon.
3. Krishna (rises at Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra) has major tributaries Tungabhadra, Bhima, Koyna, and Musi.
qe: Which of the following peninsular rivers is called 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South) and has the largest drainage basin in Peninsular India?

q: शिवालिक की तलहटी के सहारे भारत के किस भू-आकृतिक क्षेत्र को 'भाबर' (Bhabar) पेटी कहा जाता है?
o: Marshy, forested belt with dense wildlife south of pebbles
Narrow 8–16 km porous belt of coarse pebbles and boulders where Himalayan streams disappear underground
Elevated terraces of old kankar-rich alluvium
New fertile floodplains renewed annually by river silt
e:
Bhabar is the coarse pebble-strewn piedmont zone right below the Shiwaliks where streams sink underground; they re-emerge immediately south in the marshy 'Terai' belt (भाबर कंकड़-पत्थर वाली संकीर्ण पट्टी है जहाँ नदियाँ विलुप्त हो जाती हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. North-to-South sequence across Northern Plains: Shiwaliks → Bhabar → Terai → Bhangar (old alluvium) → Khadar (new alluvium).
2. In Punjab, Khadar floodplains are locally called 'Bet' (बेट).
3. Doab means fertile land between two rivers (e.g., Bist Doab: Beas–Sutlej; Bari Doab: Beas–Ravi; Ganga–Yamuna Doab).
qe: Which physiographic region of India is known as the 'Bhabar' (भाबर) belt along the foothills of the Shiwaliks?
oe: Marshy, forested belt with dense wildlife south of pebbles
Narrow 8–16 km porous belt of coarse pebbles and boulders where Himalayan streams disappear underground
Elevated terraces of old kankar-rich alluvium
New fertile floodplains renewed annually by river silt

q: भारत की कौन-सी मृदा उच्च तापमान और भारी वर्षा वाले उष्णकटिबंधीय क्षेत्रों में तीव्र निक्षालन (leaching) से बनती है, सूखने पर ईंट जैसी कठोर हो जाती है और काजू, चाय व कॉफी के लिए उपयुक्त है?
e:
Laterite (from Latin 'later' = brick) is rich in iron and aluminium oxides but poor in nitrogen, humus, and lime, found in Western Ghats, Kerala, Karnataka, Odisha, and Meghalaya (लैटेराइट मिट्टी तीव्र निक्षालन से बनती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Red & Yellow soils owe their red colour to ferric oxide diffusion in crystalline/metamorphic rocks (Deccan & Eastern Plateau).
2. Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) classifies Indian soils into 8 major groups.
3. Chambal Valley (MP/Rajasthan/UP) is notorious for severe gully erosion forming 'Ravines' (Badlands / बीहड़).
qe: Which soil type of India develops in high-temperature, high-rainfall tropical regions through intense leaching, hardens like brick upon drying, and is ideal for cashew, tea, and coffee?

q: केरल की अन्नामलाई पहाड़ियों में स्थित प्रायद्वीपीय भारत (दक्षिण भारत) की सबसे ऊँची चोटी कौन-सी है?
e:
Anamudi (2,695 m, Eravikulam NP, Kerala) is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and Peninsular India (अनाईमुडी दक्षिण भारत की सबसे ऊँची चोटी है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Doddabetta (2,637 m, Tamil Nadu) is the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills (2nd highest in South India).
2. Jindhagada Peak (1,690 m, AP) / Arma Konda & Mahendragiri (1,501 m, Odisha) are major peaks of the Eastern Ghats.
3. Western Ghats ('Sahyadri') are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of India's 4 Biodiversity Hotspots (Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Sundaland, Western Ghats).
qe: Which is the highest peak of Peninsular India (South India), located in the Anaimalai Hills of Kerala?

q: भारत में मूँगफली का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक राज्य गुजरात है; इसी प्रकार पटसन (जूट — 'गोल्डन फाइबर') के उत्पादन में भारत का कौन-सा राज्य प्रथम स्थान पर है?
e:
West Bengal produces over 75% of India's Jute ('Golden Fibre') in the fertile Hooghly–Ganga delta (पश्चिम बंगाल जूट उत्पादन में प्रथम है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. India's first modern jute mill was set up at Rishra (near Kolkata) in 1855; first successful cotton mill at Bombay (1854, Cowasji Nanabhai Davar).
2. Central Jute Technological Research Institute is in Kolkata.
3. Major leading states: Tea — Assam; Coffee — Karnataka; Rubber & Cardamom — Kerala; Sugarcane & Wheat — UP; Soyabean & Pulses — MP; Mustard — Rajasthan.
qe: Which Indian state is the largest producer of Cotton AND Groundnut in India (often competing with Maharashtra/Telangana for cotton), while West Bengal leads in which fibre crop?

q:
भारतीय मानसून के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: अल-नीनो (मध्य/पूर्वी विषुवतरेखीय प्रशांत महासागर का असामान्य तापन) सामान्यतः भारत में कमजोर या कम दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून वर्षा से जुड़ा होता है।
कथन II: सकारात्मक हिंद महासागर द्विध्रुव (Positive IOD) भारतीय दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून को मजबूत करने की प्रवृत्ति रखता है।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II
e:
Both statements are scientifically accurate: El Niño suppresses Indian monsoon (while La Niña enhances it), and a Positive IOD can even partially offset an El Niño's drying impact on India (दोनों कथन पूर्णतः सत्य हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Southwest Monsoon normally hits the Kerala coast around 1 June and withdraws from NW India starting mid-September.
2. About 75%–80% of India's total annual rainfall is delivered by the Southwest Monsoon (June–September).
3. Sir Gilbert Walker discovered the Southern Oscillation (ENSO) while serving as Director-General of Observatories in India.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Monsoon:
Statement I: El Niño (abnormal warming of central/eastern equatorial Pacific waters) is generally associated with weakened or deficient Southwest Monsoon rainfall in India.
Statement II: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD — warmer western Indian Ocean than eastern Indian Ocean) tends to strengthen the Indian Southwest Monsoon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q: भारत के निम्नलिखित परमाणु ऊर्जा संयंत्रों में से कौन-सा अपने राज्य से सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
e:
Kaiga Atomic Power Station is located in Karnataka (Uttara Kannada district on the Kali river), NOT Tamil Nadu (कैगा परमाणु संयंत्र कर्नाटक में स्थित है; तमिलनाडु में कलपक्कम और कुडनकुलम हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Tarapur (Maharashtra, 1969) is India's oldest commercial nuclear power station.
2. Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu, Russian VVER reactors) is India's largest nuclear power plant by capacity; Kalpakkam (Madras APS) is also in Tamil Nadu.
3. Narora Atomic Power Station is located in Bulandshahr district, Uttar Pradesh.
qe: Which of the following Nuclear Power Plants of India is NOT correctly matched with its state?

q:
सूची-I (बायोस्फीयर रिजर्व) को सूची-II (राज्य) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:

qe:
Match List-I (Biosphere Reserve / Tiger Reserve) with List-II (State) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Simlipal
2. Nokrek
3. Pachmarhi
4. Agasthyamalai

q: भारतीय रेलवे के किस जोन का मुख्यालय प्रयागराज (उत्तर प्रदेश) में है, तथा पूर्वोत्तर रेलवे (NER) का मुख्यालय कहाँ स्थित है?
e:
North Central Railway (NCR) is headquartered at Prayagraj, and North Eastern Railway (NER) is headquartered at Gorakhpur (उत्तर मध्य रेलवे — प्रयागराज; पूर्वोत्तर रेलवे — गोरखपुर)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Northern Railway HQ: New Delhi; East Central Railway HQ: Hajipur (Bihar).
2. Konkan Railway (Rohas to Mangaluru, 741 km) runs along the rugged Western Ghats coast.
3. Golden Quadrilateral (5,846 km) connects Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata; North–South and East–West corridors intersect at Jhansi (UP).
qe: Which railway zone of Indian Railways is headquartered at Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh), and where is the headquarters of North Eastern Railway (NER)?

q: कौन-सी नदी कश्मीर घाटी में पीर पंजाल श्रेणी की तलहटी में स्थित वेरीनाग झरने से निकलती है और श्रीनगर व वुलर झील से होकर बहती है?
e:
Jhelum (ancient Vitasta) rises at Verinag, meanders across the flat Kashmir Valley (an unusual youthful-stage meandering river due to old lake-bed Karewas), passes through Srinagar & Wular Lake, and joins Chenab in Pakistan (झेलम वेरीनाग से निकलती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Indus Water Treaty (1960, brokered by World Bank): India got unrestricted use of 3 Eastern Rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej); Pakistan got 3 Western Rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) with limited non-consumptive/hydro rights for India.
2. Chenab (Chandra + Bhaga rivers meeting at Tandi, HP) is the largest tributary of the Indus.
3. Beas is the ONLY major Indus tributary that lies entirely within Indian territory (meets Sutlej at Harike, Punjab).
qe: Which river originates from the Verinag Spring at the foot of the Pir Panjal range in Kashmir Valley and flows through Srinagar and Wular Lake?

q: राजस्थान के झुंझुनू जिले की 'खेतड़ी' पेटी और मध्य प्रदेश के बालाघाट जिले का 'मलाजखंड' भारत में किस अलौह धातु के प्रमुख खनन केंद्र हैं?
e:
Malanjkhand (MP), Khetri (Rajasthan), and Singhbhum/Ghatsila (Jharkhand) are India's three major Copper belts (खेतड़ी व मलाजखंड ताँबे के प्रमुख खनन क्षेत्र हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Zawar mines (Udaipur, Rajasthan) are famous for Lead and Zinc.
2. Panna (Madhya Pradesh) is India's only active industrial Diamond mine.
3. Balaghat (MP) and Nagpur–Bhandara (Maharashtra) are also major Manganese belts.
qe: The 'Khetri' belt in Jhunjhunu district of Rajasthan and 'Malanjkhand' in Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh are India's premier mining hubs for which non-ferrous metal?

q: भारत की कौन-सी भूगर्भिक शैल प्रणाली सर्वाधिक धात्विक खनिजों (लौह अयस्क, मैंगनीज, ताँबा, सोना) से समृद्ध है?
e:
The Dharwar System (metamorphosed Archean sedimentary rocks, named after Dharwar district in Karnataka) is economically the richest metallic-mineral rock system in India (धारवाड़ क्रम धात्विक खनिजों में सर्वाधिक समृद्ध है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Gondwana System holds ~98% of India's coal reserves.
2. Vindhyan System is famous for building stones (red sandstone used in Red Fort, Sanchi Stupa, Fatehpur Sikri), limestone, and Panna/Golconda diamonds.
3. Deccan Trap (Cretaceous basaltic lava flows) weathered into fertile Black Cotton Soil (Regur).
qe: Which geological rock system of India is the oldest (Precambrian basement complex) and richest in metallic minerals like iron ore, manganese, copper, and gold (Kolar/Dharwar)?

q: राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग विकास परियोजना का उत्तर-दक्षिण कॉरिडोर (श्रीनगर-कन्याकुमारी) और पूर्व-पश्चिम कॉरिडोर (सिलचर-पोरबंदर) उत्तर प्रदेश के किस नगर में एक-दूसरे को काटते हैं?
e:
The North–South and East–West Highway Corridors intersect at Jhansi in the Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh (उत्तर-दक्षिण और पूर्व-पश्चिम गलियारे झाँसी में एक-दूसरे को काटते हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was established in 1988 (operationalized 1995) under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
2. Bharatmala Pariyojana is India's flagship umbrella highway development programme.
3. India has the second-largest road network in the world (after the USA).
qe: Which city in Uttar Pradesh lies at the intersection of the North–South Corridor (Srinagar–Kanyakumari) and East–West Corridor (Silchar–Porbandar) of NHAI?
